evals.name: correct-but-terse-is-left-alone
evals.setup: `Get`'s godoc is a single accurate sentence that already states the one thing the signature cannot — that a miss returns the zero value rather than an error.
expected_behavior: Runs the checklist and finds that no item fires
Leaves the comment byte-for-byte unchanged — no padding, no restating the signature
Reports no change line for it; shortness alone is not a defect

evals.name: adds-only-confirmable-facts
evals.setup: `Store` mutates the slice it is passed and its body suggests it is safe for concurrent use, but nothing in the code proves the concurrency claim. Its godoc states neither.
expected_behavior: Fires the missing-fact checklist item for the mutation and for concurrency
Confirms each against the body and its callers (via `LSP`) before writing it
Documents the slice mutation, which the code proves
Flags the concurrency safety as unverifiable rather than asserting it in the godoc

evals.name: directives-and-interface-method-godoc
evals.setup: `./pkg/io` carries a `//go:build` line, a `//go:generate` directive, and a `Read` method implementing `io.Reader` whose godoc restates the interface contract and nothing more.
expected_behavior: Leaves both directive comments byte-for-byte unchanged and lists them as never-touch items in the plan
Plans the `Read` godoc for removal as unremarkable — it would be kept, naming the surprise, only if `Read` broke or exceeded the `io.Reader` contract
Writes nothing before approval, since a package target is plan-first

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup: An ordinary single-function run that changes one godoc and deletes one inline comment.
expected_behavior: Opens with the result — no preamble and no narration of reading the code
Lists changes made as `file:Symbol — item`, plus flagged and never-touched items, each stated once
No closing restatement of the edits it just listed

evals.name: line-target-resolves-to-its-item
evals.setup: Line 42 of `pkg/svc/foo.go` is inside the body of `(*Svc).Flush`, where `// increment i` sits above `i++`. The file holds four other functions.
expected_behavior: States the resolved kind (line) and the item: `Flush`'s godoc and its body's inline comments — nothing else in the file
Presents no plan; a line target is a single item, so it runs the loop straight through
Deletes `// increment i` as a comment that only restates the code

evals.name: module-mode-with-fanout-and-filter
evals.setup: A module of eleven packages, two of them `svc` and `api`.
expected_behavior: The plan lists items from `svc` and `api` only; every other package is reported as skipped
After approval, dispatches one subagent per package and merges their reports into the skill's output format
Verifies each edited package with `gofmt -l` and `go build` before reporting
